title: Cardinal Billing Account Terms: Refunds, Small-Balance Write-Offs, Collections and Account Close
content:
These terms of the Cardinal Billing Account govern what happens to a credit or debit balance that is left on the account.

**Refund of a credit balance.** A credit balance is refunded within the pay plan's refund issue days after it arises when the policy has ended or when the plan does not hold overpayments. Credits of payments by check or EFT are refunded only after the pay plan's check clearing days (business days) from the payment.

**Where a refund goes.** A refund goes to the electronic method that paid where the pay plan refunds to the original method and that method is a card or bank account; otherwise it is sent by check to the mailing address.

**Write-off at close.** At account close a credit below the pay plan's smallest refundable credit and a debit up to the pay plan's largest small-balance write-off are written off.

**Collections.** A final earned-premium balance at or above the pay plan's smallest collections balance that is still unpaid the pay plan's collections referral days after the cancellation effective date is referred to collections. A balance in collections that is paid closes the account.

**Close.** An account closes only after the policy has ended and the balance is zero.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical figures, plan minimum refund $5.00, write-off ceiling $4.99, collections minimum $25.00)

| Balance at close or after cancellation | Result |
|---|---|
| Credit of $4.80 at close | Written off |
| Credit of $5.00 at close | Refunded |
| Debit of $4.99 at close | Written off |
| Debit of $5.00 at close | Not written off under this rule |
| Final earned-premium balance of $30.00 still unpaid at the referral day | Referred to collections |
| Final earned-premium balance of $20.00 still unpaid at the referral day | Not referred; it is below the minimum |

**Refund destination, illustrated.** A credit paid by debit card on a plan that refunds to the original method goes back to that debit card; a credit paid by money order goes by check to the mailing address, since a money order is neither a card nor a bank account.
